Subject: Proposed DPA addendum: staggered deletion windows & subprocessor handshake

Hi team — attaching a short DPA addendum proposal that captures the "staggered deletion window" approach we discussed on the call. The core ask from Belmont was: allow a short, bounded delay between primary deletion and final backup purge to support disaster recovery + legal holds, while still meeting your data subject erasure obligations.

Key points in the draft: 
- Primary dataset deletion within 30 days of request, where feasible.
- Backup purge executed in stages: immutable snapshot tombstone at 30 days, full purge within 90 days by default.
- Emergency freeze clause (audit/legal hold) to pause purge for up to 14 days on valid request, with notification and minimal access logging.
- Subprocessor disclosure/handshake: we list our backup subprocessor (Acme Backup, Inc.) and propose a 30-day notice for subprocessor rotation or cross-border transfer.

Please review the attached PDF (dpa_addendum_staggered_purge_v1.pdf). Karthik and Laura are copied for technical and operational confirmation — Karthik will add suggested language for log TTLs and restore escrow.

Proposed next steps: Belmont legal reviews + we accept minor redlines or flag issues for a 15-min sync. If OK, we will provide a DocuSign envelope for signature.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Legal Operations (Contracts)
Redwood Inference

Kim — thanks for the quick turnaround and the draft. A couple of clarifying questions before we escalate to our internal counsel: 

1) When you say "immutable snapshot tombstone at 30 days," do you mean that the snapshot is logically marked and remains available for forensic restore for the full 90-day period? Who can trigger a restore request during that window?

2) The emergency freeze clause sounds reasonable. We need explicit SLAs on notification and an audit trail for any freeze/unfreeze action. Can you propose the exact metadata you plan to log?

3) We also require a list of subprocessors who will potentially access backups for restore operations — not just the storage provider. The draft only names Acme Backup (storage). Please confirm whether any other vendors (e.g., restore orchestration, vendor-managed snapshots) might have access.

We can probably accept a staggered purge as an operational compromise, but legal will want clear timing and minimal operator access during the tombstone period.

Regards,
Maya Singh
Senior Counsel, Data Privacy
Belmont Health

On Wed, Aug 22, 2028 at 9:13 AM Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi team — attaching a short DPA addendum proposal that captures the "staggered deletion window" approach we discussed on the call.

Maya / Belmont — quick technical clarifications below (copied into the draft as tracked comments in the redline doc):

1) Tombstone semantics and restore scope: The "tombstone" is metadata we attach to immutable snapshots. Snapshots are retained in object storage but flagged. By default only a narrow restore API is available to our internal On-Call Runbook service; restores are gated behind a documented incident/customer request flow and require two-person approval when triggered during the tombstone period. In the addendum we'll propose: restores require a documented request + approval from both Redwood Ops and a Belmont authorized contact.

2) Audit logs & metadata: We propose logging the following for any freeze/unfreeze/restore action: actor identity, timestamp, action type, justification, ticket/reference id, snapshot id, and TTL at action time. Logs are retained per our standard log retention policy (default 365 days) but we can surface a copy for Belmont in the event of an audit.

3) Subprocessors: Operationally, the backup stack includes: Acme Backup (object storage + lifecycle), VaultOps (restore orchestration) and SnapshotBridge (cross-region replication). In normal operations only Acme has direct access to raw snapshot blobs; VaultOps holds orchestration-level tokens to request restores and SnapshotBridge is a managed service for replication. We can add a clause that any subprocessor with restore capability will require Belmont-specific access controls and notification within 30 days of onboarding.

I've attached a redline with this language (redline_dpa_addendum_karthik_comments.docx). I'm flexible on the exact day counts but recommend keeping the tombstone <= 90 days so we don't run afoul of erasure timelines while providing a reasonable recovery window.

-Karthik
Principal Product Manager, Reliability
Redwood Inference

Maya — thanks for the questions. Per Karthik's notes, summarizing the operational commitments we can accept and the limited exceptions we propose in the DPA addendum:

- Deletion cadence: primary dataset deletion attempted within 30 days of verified request; backups flagged (tombstone) and subject to purge within 90 days.
- Restore gating: two-person approval during tombstone window; Belmont must designate an authorized restore contact list in the onboarding packet.
- Emergency freeze: Redwood will accept formal legal freeze requests from Belmont; freeze/unfreeze actions will be logged (actor, time, justification, ticket id) and we will notify Belmont within 4 business hours of action.
- Subprocessor disclosures: we will include Acme Backup, VaultOps, SnapshotBridge and will require 30-day notice for onboarding or cross-border changes.

If that matches Belmont's expectations, we can incorporate the exact wording Karthik proposed and send a redlined PDF / DocuSign. Would you prefer a short 15-min sync to finish wording or for us to circulate the redline first?

Best,

If you can add those tweaks and send the redline, legal will sign off. We prefer DocuSign for execution.
